# Build workflows that travel

[← Main guide](../README.md) · [Browse resources](resources.md)

Workflow engineering is shared across scientific tracks. Learn one engine first, then use a familiar analysis to understand dependencies, portability, and failure recovery.

## Along this path

- [From scripts to reproducible workflows](#workflow-concepts)
- [Nextflow and nf-core](#nextflow)

<a id="workflow-concepts"></a>

## From scripts to reproducible workflows

**Level:** Intermediate

Learn the common ideas before committing to a particular engine.

**Before you begin:** Shell basics, a working analysis script, and software environments.

### What to understand

- Tasks, input/output contracts, dependency graphs, and configuration.
- Versioned software, containers, sample sheets, resource declarations, and logs.
- Small fixtures, expected outputs, restart behavior, and provenance.

### What you’ll be able to do

Draw and implement a small analysis as a dependency graph.

### Try this

Run the workflow-basics project as a plain Python script, then reproduce its expected output with one engine.

### Keep in mind

A workflow engine cannot repair unclear scientific assumptions or an incorrect analysis step. Validate the underlying computation first.

### A few good resources

- [Nextflow documentation](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow) — Documentation · Intermediate · Free; compute may cost · English. Reference processes, channels, modules, profiles, executors, and dependency handling while building a small pipeline.
  - Prerequisites: Command-line use and workflow concepts.

- [Snakemake documentation](https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) — Documentation · Intermediate · Free; compute may cost · English. Understand rules, file dependencies, software environments, execution, and reporting.
  - Prerequisites: Basic Python and command-line use.

- [nf-core documentation](https://nf-co.re/docs/) — Documentation · Intermediate · Free · English. Learn conventions for using and developing community pipelines, including configuration and contribution guidance.
  - Prerequisites: Nextflow basics.

- [Apptainer user guide](https://apptainer.org/docs/user/latest/) — Documentation · Intermediate · Free; infrastructure may cost · English. Learn container execution and reproducibility concepts relevant to shared research computing systems.
  - Prerequisites: Linux and software environment basics.

<a id="nextflow"></a>

## Nextflow and nf-core

**Level:** Intermediate

Run, configure, and develop portable pipelines using dataflow concepts.

**Before you begin:** Workflow concepts and command-line experience.

### What to understand

- Processes, channels, workflow composition, and modules.
- Parameters, profiles, containers, executors, and resume behavior.
- Using nf-core pipelines and understanding their documentation and quality conventions.

### What you’ll be able to do

Run a small Nextflow workflow, change a parameter, and explain its task dependencies.

### Try this

Complete the official introductory training, then run main.nf in the workflow-basics project and compare its output with the reference file.

### Keep in mind

Start with a small local test profile. Check the data, storage, and compute requirements before running a production pipeline.

### A few good resources

- [Nextflow community training](https://training.nextflow.io/) — Course · Intermediate · Free · English. A guided route from running a first pipeline to composing and configuring workflows.
  - Prerequisites: Basic shell skills; start with the introductory material.

- [Nextflow documentation](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow) — Documentation · Intermediate · Free; compute may cost · English. Reference processes, channels, modules, profiles, executors, and dependency handling while building a small pipeline.
  - Prerequisites: Command-line use and workflow concepts.

- [nf-core documentation](https://nf-co.re/docs/) — Documentation · Intermediate · Free · English. Learn conventions for using and developing community pipelines, including configuration and contribution guidance.
  - Prerequisites: Nextflow basics.

- [nf-core/rnaseq](https://nf-co.re/rnaseq) — Workflow · Intermediate · Code free; compute and storage may cost · English. A production workflow to examine after a smaller tutorial; learn its inputs, profiles, QC outputs, and documented options.
  - Prerequisites: RNA-seq concepts, Nextflow, and suitable compute access.

<a id="snakemake"></a>

## Snakemake

**Level:** Intermediate

Express analysis steps as rules connected through their input and output files.

**Before you begin:** Workflow concepts and basic Python.

### What to understand

- Rules, targets, wildcards, configuration, and dependency graphs.
- Software environments, containers, resource declarations, and execution profiles.
- Dry runs, logs, reports, and testing small examples.

### What you’ll be able to do

Write a small rule-based workflow and inspect what will run before executing it.

### Try this

Run a dry run and then the Snakefile in the workflow-basics project. Change the input FASTA and predict which output should be recomputed.

### Keep in mind

Make all dependencies explicit. Hidden files, undeclared parameters, and changing environments undermine reproducibility.

### A few good resources

- [Snakemake documentation](https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) — Documentation · Intermediate · Free; compute may cost · English. Understand rules, file dependencies, software environments, execution, and reporting.
  - Prerequisites: Basic Python and command-line use.

- [Snakemake general-use tutorial](https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorial/tutorial.html) — Tutorial · Intermediate · Free · English. Build and extend an example workflow while learning dependency handling, configuration, and execution.
  - Prerequisites: Basic Python and shell use.

- [Apptainer user guide](https://apptainer.org/docs/user/latest/) — Documentation · Intermediate · Free; infrastructure may cost · English. Learn container execution and reproducibility concepts relevant to shared research computing systems.
  - Prerequisites: Linux and software environment basics.
